text: There was no sunrise this morning. The only light on the river comes from the lamps along the quay.
People hurry inside. On the road along the water, the traffic slowly comes to a stop.
One driver steps out, and looks up at a sky that should be blue.
Right now, almost every heater and every light is switched on at the same time.
Power grids were never built for a night without end. Within hours, they are pushed past their limits.
And then, one by one, the lights go out.
Without the Sun, the ground keeps losing its heat to space, and nothing comes to replace it.
By midnight, your breath turns white in the air.
On a clear night, the temperature can drop a degree or two every hour. This night will never end.
At the edges of the river, the water begins to freeze. Frost creeps over the cars. The trees turn white.
And now, the real danger begins.
